subject: Pilot workload envelope & sizing - follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Alex Green <alex.green@scaleworks.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot workload envelope & sizing - follow-up and next steps

Alex — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick post-call recap and a small set of clarifying questions so we can lock a sizing estimate for the pilot. Attachment: workload_profile.csv (sample event rates + payload sizes).

Summary of what we heard on the call:
- Latency target: p95 <= 300ms for single-turn generation (non-streaming).
- Streaming requirement: long-lived streaming sessions for multi-turn assistant with incremental token writes; target first-byte <= 150ms for streaming responses.
- Throughput: baseline steady-state ~45 QPS sustained, average payload ~900 tokens per request.
- Peak pattern: several 30-minute bursts daily; 10x multiplier during marketing pushes — observed peak QPS ~450 for 12-18 minutes.
- Concurrency: expected concurrent streaming sessions ~120 active sessions during peaks.

Clarifying asks (can you confirm quickly?):
1) Are the 900 token numbers including or excluding context/prompt tokens? We assumed total input+output tokens in the CSV.
2) For streaming sessions, do you expect partial responses to be sent frequently (every ~50 tokens) or batched larger chunks? This affects kv-cache behavior.
3) Any hard constraints on regional routing (we assumed US-only for pilot)?

What we'll do next from Redwood:
- Produce a sizing proposal (throughput / GPU sizing / fallback policy) by EOD Wednesday based on the CSV.
- Propose a configuration for streaming sessions (chunking, keepalive) so we meet first-byte SLO.
- Draft a short mutual action plan with milestones and a proposed 30-day pilot SLA.

Thanks — if you can reply inline to the questions above it'll speed things up.

— Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Alex Green <alex.green@scaleworks.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: ScaleWorks Sales <sales@scaleworks.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot workload envelope & sizing - follow-up and next steps

Sergio — appreciate the recap and clear asks. Quick answers: 
1) Token accounting: the 900 token number I gave on the call includes the model input + expected generation (so total end-to-end). We can split if you prefer separate columns.
2) Streaming chunks: we stream incremental partials roughly every 40–80 tokens depending on user interaction (typical is ~60 tokens). First-byte latency is critical for perceived interactivity — sub-200ms ideal.
3) Region: pilot traffic will be US-only for the first 90 days, yes.

I'll attach a small sample of live payloads (sample_payloads.json) so you can see distribution by user type. One more data point: our background reranking calls run asynchronously at higher QPS (about 2x the generation QPS) but are non-streaming and can tolerate p95 <= 600ms.

Happy to join a technical sizing call if needed.

— Alex
Alex Green
Head of Product Engineering, ScaleWorks
alex.green@scaleworks.com | +1 (212) 555-0199

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Green <alex.green@scaleworks.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 08:31:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Pilot workload envelope & sizing - follow-up and next steps

Alex / team — thanks for the quick clarifications and for the sample payloads. I've sketched an initial Redwood sizing estimate and attached the PDF (redwood_sizing_estimate_v1.pdf). High-level notes from our sizing exercise: 

- Baseline steady-state: assume 45 QPS * 900 tokens => ~40k tokens/sec. With efficient batching and prefix caching we estimate 2x token throughput per GPU for non-streaming paths; for streaming paths (low-latency first-byte) we allocate more headroom.
- Peak sizing (10x bursts to 450 QPS): short 12–18 minute windows where we recommend enabling burst capacity with pre-warmed instances and elastic routing. We modeled an autoscale profile that brings additional dedicated pods online within ~90s to hit peak within SLA.
- Concurrency: concurrent streaming sessions ~120 requires keeping KV cache capacity per session; we recommend a streaming-optimized pool sized at ~150 sessions to allow buffer for tail.
- Fallback policy: when sustained burst > 20min we recommend graceful degradation to a smaller model variant for speculative responses to preserve latency SLOs.

Open questions before we finalize numbers: 
- Confirm steady-state QPS distribution across hours (attached CSV has hour buckets — any mismatches?)
- How important is preserving generation quality across fallbacks vs. strict latency? We can tune quantization/model variant choices based on preference.

Next steps proposed:
1) Technical deep-dive (30–45m) with your infra/eng team — propose Wed 13 Oct 10:30am PT.
2) Sign off on pilot SLA and burst policy — we can draft in parallel.
3) Pilot kickoff: capture test plan + success metrics.

If that time works, I'll send an invite and a short agenda.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Alex / Marissa — thanks both. Wed 13 Oct 10:30am PT works for our team (I'll send invite). Quick confirmations before the call: 
- Marissa: please include the autoscale timing assumptions and the model-variant fallback matrix in the PDF so the engineering team can evaluate impact on quality.
- Alex: we'll treat reranking workload as asynchronous backfill — that reduces immediate GPU pressure for streaming pool. If you can, mark any high-priority reranking customers in the CSV.

Planned agenda for Wed (30–45m):
1) Walk the CSV distributions and sample payloads (5–10m)
2) Sizing assumptions & autoscale profile (Marissa) (10–12m)
3) Streaming session behavior & keepalive/chunking tuning (Ben) (8–10m)
4) Action items: pilot SLA draft, measurement plan, sign-off owners (5m)

Action items going into the call:
- Redwood: final sizing deck and Doc with fallback matrix (Marissa).
- ScaleWorks: annotate CSV with any prioritized customers + confirm avg tokens per user type (Alex).
- Sergio: calendar invite + Tech-Deep agenda.

I'll include a short runbook (how we instrument p95 and streaming first-byte) and the DocuSign link for the pilot agreement in the invite.

See you Wed — Sergio
